assets.brief: The Crypt: cool blue-grey cut stone, ossuary niches with skulls, cracked flagstones, iron braziers and candle light (warm against cool), cobwebs, cracked sarcophagi; undead resting place. Materials: blue-grey cut stone, bone-white accents (never pure white), warm candle amber. Same biome look in every cell; overhead three-quarter top-down camera like the shared dungeon boss sheets; chunky Metal Slug-era painterly rendering; dark overall; no characters; no text. FLOOR TILES: SQUARE tile-shaped pieces with hard straight cut edges, flat even lighting (NO vignette, NO baked shadows, NO bright centre) so they tile seamlessly side by side; a quiet readable floor that never fights the characters on top.
assets.geometry: Tile 16 px (v1) / 32 px (v2) per grid cell; rooms are 24x14 tiles.
assets.name: The Crypt floor tiles
assets.need: Seamless variants for a 16 px-tile grid (art sampled down from rich source).
assets.states: cell1-6=six seamless floor tile variants (plain, worn, cracked, patched, stained, rich); cell7-8=two edge/border-trim tiles (floor meeting wall, with a dark shadow edge on top); cell9-12=four decals (a crack, a puddle or stain, scattered debris, a biome-specific detail) on transparent alpha

Same biome look in every cell; overhead three-quarter top-down camera like the shared dungeon boss sheets; chunky Metal Slug-era painterly rendering; dark overall; no characters; no text. WALL PIECES: the walls of a flip-screen room seen from the camera: the NORTH wall shows its tall FACE (about 1.5 tiles tall with a lit top cap) and the other walls show their top cap and a short face. Wide pieces, hard straight cut sides so they tile left-right.

assets.brief: The Crypt: cool blue-grey cut stone, ossuary niches with skulls, iron braziers and candle light. Materials: blue-grey cut stone, bone accents (never pure white), warm candle amber. STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC, AXIS-ALIGNED, overhead three-quarter as in a classic 16-bit top-down action game: the NORTH wall is drawn in straight-on FRONT ELEVATION; side (west/east) and south walls are shown ONLY as flat TOP-DOWN CAP STRIPS. Every edge is exactly horizontal or vertical: NO vanishing point, NO 45-degree rotation, NO isometric cube, NO visible diagonal side face, NO angled or diagonal pieces anywhere. Same biome look in every cell; chunky Metal Slug-era painterly rendering; dark overall (walls mean value about 25-35%, no highlights above 70%); no characters; no text. Every cell the same size; alpha strictly 0 or 255, no soft haze. WALL SET: pieces must butt seamlessly left-to-right (or top-to-bottom for side caps) with NO irregular pilaster at the tile edges.
assets.geometry: Wall faces 1 x 1.5 tiles; caps 1 tile (16 px v1 / 32 px v2).

assets.need: Grid-ready orthogonal wall/door pieces for an axis-aligned 24x14 room.

assets.brief: Dragon Keep: slate-blue basalt fortress masonry with thin orange lava cracks, iron chains and grates. Materials: slate and basalt blue-grey, a little orange lava glow (only in cracks), iron. STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC, AXIS-ALIGNED, overhead three-quarter as in a classic 16-bit top-down action game: the NORTH wall is drawn in straight-on FRONT ELEVATION; side (west/east) and south walls are shown ONLY as flat TOP-DOWN CAP STRIPS. Every edge is exactly horizontal or vertical: NO vanishing point, NO 45-degree rotation, NO isometric cube, NO visible diagonal side face, NO angled or diagonal pieces anywhere. Same biome look in every cell; chunky Metal Slug-era painterly rendering; dark overall (walls mean value about 25-35%, no highlights above 70%); no characters; no text. Every cell the same size; alpha strictly 0 or 255, no soft haze. DOORS AND STAIRS: the room is fought behind BARRED doors (iron bars / thorn barrier / biome equivalent), open after. The north door is straight-on front elevation; west/east/south doors are flat top-down: a gap in the cap strip with the bars seen from above as a row of posts.
